description: A high-school principal must approve the operating protocol for a student newspaper, including its publication channel, frequency, editorial review, commenting, and interview-consent rules, with input from the journalism adviser, district legal liaison, instructional technology coordinator, and school counselor.

shared_context.S1: The student newspaper is ready for its first issue of the school year.
shared_context.S2: The current draft proposes a weekly paper-only publication with principal approval of each issue before distribution.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Morgan has authority to approve the newspaper's operating protocol.
shared_context.S4: The school's routine approval meeting hears from the journalism adviser, legal liaison, instructional technology coordinator, and counselor before the principal signs a student-publication plan.

PF1.text: The student editorial board formally adopted a monthly publication cycle because its available editing and layout staff can complete one issue every four weeks; Ms. Rivera recorded the vote in the club minutes, but the draft protocol still says weekly.

PF2.text: The district student-expression policy forbids principal prepublication approval and requires a correction notice to be posted within exactly 5 school days after a verified error; Mr. Chen confirmed the current policy wording during his legal review, but the draft still uses the older approval language.

PF3.text: The district's supported publication platform is the school CMS, which requires district single-sign-on accounts and can be configured only with public comments disabled; Ms. Okafor tested the configuration this week, but the draft was prepared before that test.

PF4.text: The editorial board plans to interview minors about personal experiences with grief and family crisis, and the school counseling protocol requires written guardian consent before publishing any such interview; Mr. Bennett confirmed the protocol with the counseling team this week, but it is not in the publication draft.

acceptance_conditions: The newspaper must publish through the school CMS.
The publication frequency must be monthly.
The protocol must use post-publication correction review rather than principal prepublication approval.
A verified error must receive a correction notice within exactly 5 school days.
Access must use district single sign-on.
Written guardian consent must be required before publishing a sensitive interview.
A formal student-publication protocol record must be created.

content_checks.C1: 'school CMS' in decisions['publication_channel'] or 'School CMS' in decisions['publication_channel']
content_checks.C3: 'no principal prepublication approval' in decisions['editorial_review_process'] or 'No principal prepublication approval' in decisions['editorial_review_process']
content_checks.C7: 'written guardian consent' in decisions['sensitive_interview_consent'] or 'Written guardian consent' in decisions['sensitive_interview_consent']
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] in ['student_publication_protocol', 'protocol_revision', 'revision', 'policy_compliance', 'platform_specification', 'student_safeguard', 'final_approval', 'final_review'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The editorial board's recorded staffing decision changes the publication frequency from the draft's weekly cycle to exactly monthly.
The confirmed district policy changes review from principal prepublication approval to post-publication correction and sets the correction deadline at exactly 5 school days.
The tested CMS configuration changes the channel to the school CMS, disables public comments, and requires district single-sign-on access.
The counseling protocol changes the interview rule from unrestricted publication to written guardian consent before publishing sensitive interviews with minors.
